newsitem.title: GERMANY: Strike action hits NATO army bases in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Strike action hits NATO army bases in Germany.

text.p: Thousands of German civilian workers at NATO members' army bases in Germany carried out strike action on Tuesday to protest against cost-cutting measures by their employers, unions said.

More than 4,000 employees took part in the strikes, a spokeswoman for the German public sector union OeTV said. The strike action will continue until Friday, while talks on cost-cutting measures will reopen on Wednesday.

Around 35,000 civilians, mostly German, are employed by the NATO allies across the country. An earlier six-week strike involved some 3,000 workers. The union said many of the 35,000 jobs were threatened by the rationalisation measures.
The union said on Monday that many workers feared that U.S. army forces who control most of the bases were trying to "kick their staff out on to the street."
The OeTV said it drew this conclusion from a questionnaire handed to some 6,500 staff by the U.S. army base management relating to possible compensation measures.
Many civilians working at the bases have already lost their jobs as NATO forces in Germany have been cut back since the end of the Cold War.
